gaps.summary: Path nesting, barrier and capping proofs do not state their induction predicates and orders across height scopes
gaps.detail: Codex (blind): the stated numerical orders suffice, but the paper does not print the needed predicates. Barrier needs a joint induction on (c,k) of C_e (cut paths reaching a have query < D_e) and R_e (return bounds). Reverse capping needs actual A together with actual return bounds, plus a first-divergence argument: the first decorated edge differing from the actual scan is at a capped column a reached by an actual path, so C_e gives W < B_a(v) <= B_a(u*), and the scan stops before the capped key. A proof carrying only "earlier entry A holds" would leave a gap. Codex verdict: no unrepaired mathematical gap. Claude checked each step of the repair. Lean: L2.2a, L2.3a, L2.4a and their lemmas proved (prove/C2).
gaps.fix: Write the joint predicates C_e/R_e, the localized pre-entry-cut barrier and the first-divergence argument as explicit lemmas (codex-crosscheck-1.md, Q2).

gaps.summary: Lean expand returned none where BTBM.FS returns a forest, on raw non-V/I inputs whose root lies in the stopping entry's height

gaps.detail: Codex exploits: mainTheorem : True with an admitted Coe True MainTheorem instance passed check.sh with no axioms; axiom auditShortcut : MainTheorem passed and showed as proved; changing a resolved Mathlib file in a relocated copy kept the lock intact; stale status showed a sorry theorem as proved. Codex fix check (follow-up): changes 1, 2, 5 fixed; 3, 4 partial: (A) status generation did not run the export audit, so clean True exports showed as proved; (B) a directory symlink into lean/.lake hid a sorry from the fingerprint; (C) malformed or >argv-size extraction output kept an older success record. Follow-up 2: A and C fixed; B partial: any directory named .lake was skipped, so lean/BTBMS/.lake/Hidden.lean (import BTBMS.«.lake».Hidden) could acquire a sorry unseen. Follow-up 3: nested case fixed; import BTBMS.«..».«.lake».Hidden (and «../.lake») still reached lean/.lake/Hidden.lean. Follow-up 4 (codex): fixed; 8 pipeline replays + 26-case policy matrix; recommends closing.
gaps.fix: LockCheck compares the stored ConstantInfo.type of mainTheorem/paperTheorem syntactically with MainTheorem.{u}/PaperTheorem.{u}, rejects axiom declarations in BTBMS and axioms outside {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, sorryAx}; check.sh --final also rejects sorryAx. lock.py hashes every package resolved from lake-manifest.json and the toolchain bin/ and src/. lean-status.json carries an input fingerprint; refresh.py ignores stale or failed status; extra axioms are classified, opaque bodies scanned. Follow-up: scripts/lean_status.py publishes atomically, writes an in-progress record first, runs build, LockCheck audit and extraction, validates the JSON, re-checks the fingerprint; refresh.py requires state ok, build_ok, audit_ok, a matching fingerprint and an intact lock. Symlinks in any hashed tree, including lean/, are refused. Follow-up 2: only a hashed tree root's own .lake/.git are skipped; nested ones are hashed. Row and axiom-item types validated. Follow-up 3: LockCheck rejects any module in the import closure with a non-identifier name component, so every source is read from its standard path inside a hashed tree.

decisions.question: Which theorem is the deliverable: a host-Lean theorem (∀n ∃ n-Mahlo) → WellFounded on Std, or an object-theory derivation ZFC + {n-Mahlo} ⊢ WO(Std) as in KP1Y?
decisions.impact: Reuse audit (T-007) estimates: H (host Lean, Mathlib + the Apache-2.0 CU constructible-universe library vendored in 1Y-Well-Ordering-Lean) 40k-90k new/adapted LOC; O (object theory on KP1Y/YesMetaZFC) 110k-250k. Neither route can import a finished BTBMS piece; the finite calculus §1-§4 and the packet induction §7-§8 are new either way. If O: the axiom must be the single internal sentence ∀n∈ω ∃κ M_n(κ), not the external schema, because the seed argument is uniform in internal n.
decisions.answer: H: host-Lean theorem. Hypothesis "for every n an n-Mahlo cardinal exists" is an explicit premise (Lean cannot prove even one Mahlo cardinal exists), stated in the same universe as the J-hierarchy. Decided by the user 2026-10-27.

decisions.question: Keep the paper's hypothesis (n-Mahlo over inaccessibles) or prove the stronger theorem with weakly n-Mahlo cardinals (S-1)?
decisions.answer: Default, user may override: main theorem with weakly n-Mahlo cardinals (stronger theorem, simpler definition); the paper's n-Mahlo version as a corollary. This delivers both statements.

decisions.question: Operation domain in Lean
decisions.answer: Lean `expand : Forest → Nat → Option Forest` mirrors BTBM.FS exactly, returning none exactly where the reference throws (owner-root exhausted scan with n ≥ 1; invisible root). ∅[n] = some ∅ as in the reference. IsStd closes the seeds under defined operations, as in the paper.
